title: Introduce provisional-anchor-smoothing and deferred fail-fast CI hook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add provisional-anchor-smoothing to reduce brittle prompt-anchor regressions; introduce a deferred fail-fast CI hook that quarantines transient failures and escalates only after configurable windows.
description:
Context: Several prompt-set regression investigations in the last quarter (see ENG-2309) traced failures to brittle token anchors and sharp binary gating in CI. Hard-failing CI on single-anchor regressions causes noisy rollbacks and blocks teams even when signal is transient. This PR introduces two cooperating changes: (1) a provisional-anchor-smoothing adapter for eval scoring that probabilistically reweights prompt anchors to reduce single-anchor volatility, and (2) a deferred fail-fast CI hook that performs soft-fail quarantining and escalation windows before treating a regression as blocking.

What it does (high level):
- provisional anchor smoothing: adds eval pipeline logic to compute a smoothed-anchor weight for each anchor in a prompt set, implemented as a temperature-controlled softmax over anchor influence scores with optional per-cohort priors. This is pluggable via the existing eval adapter registry and can be toggled per-prompt-set.
- deferred fail-fast hook: a CI-side adapter that receives eval run outcomes and applies a short quarantine/backoff policy (configurable window in minutes and replay count). The hook will mark a run as soft-failed and schedule targeted replay sampling; only after N corroborating soft-fails within the window does it convert to a hard fail and surface to the blocking gate.

Why: Reduces false-positive regressions from single-anchor noise, improves developer signal-to-noise, and gives on-call and triage automation time to collect corroborating evidence or clear noisy anomalies without immediately blocking mainline merges.

Design notes / how it integrates:
- The smoothing algorithm exposes parameters: smoothing_temperature, anchor_prior_decay, min_effect_size. Defaults chosen after backtesting on historical prompt-sets (see docs/rfc/provisional-anchor-smoothing.md in this PR).
- The hook is written to integrate with existing CI adapter interface (ci/hooks/registry). It emits structured telemetry (soft_fail_count, quarantine_window, replay_job_id) to the eval orchestration logs so the Console can visualize soft-fail timelines.
- Backwards compatible: smoothing is opt-in at prompt-set metadata level; hook has a default non-blocking mode during a gradual rollout.

Testing:
- Unit tests: test_anchor_smoother covers temperature extremes, decay behavior, and edge cases for single-anchor prompt-sets.
- Integration tests: added an emulated CI run pipeline test that exercises quarantine and escalation logic with deterministic time acceleration.
- Backtest: included a small backtest harness and results under docs/backtests showing a 38% reduction in one-off anchor-triggered hard failures across sampled historical prompt-sets.

Changes included (summary of files):
- eval_harness/hooks/provisional_anchor_smoother.py (core algorithm + registry adapter)
- eval_harness/ci_hooks/deferred_fail_fast.py (CI adapter implementing quarantine and replay scheduling)
- eval_harness/config/defaults.yaml (new flags under eval.smoothing and ci.deferred_fail_fast)
- tests/unit/test_anchor_smoother.py (unit tests)
- tests/integration/test_deferred_fail_fast_quarantine.py (integration)
- docs/rfc/provisional-anchor-smoothing.md (design + backtest summary)
- examples/prompt_sets/anchor_weighted_example.yaml (manifest showing opt-in metadata)
- scripts/backtest/run_anchor_backtest.py (small backtest harness)

Commits (high level):
- 1a2b3c4: initial scaffolding and RFC draft added
- 4d5e6f7: implement provisional_anchor_smoother and basic unit tests
- 7f8g9h0: add CI deferred_fail_fast hook and integration harness
- 9a0b1c2: wire defaults and example prompt-set opt-in; docs/backtest results
- d3e4f5g: test hardening after reviewer feedback, CI flake fixes

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam: asked for clarification on how smoothing interacts with ensemble scoring and whether weights would bias recall-sensitive metrics. Requested an explicit test and a short doc clarifying bias tradeoffs.
- Author (Maya): responded with math derivation and added tests that assert no systematic recall bias under representative synthetic distributions; pointed to doc section 3.2.
- Priya: requested quotas on replay scheduling to avoid CI storming during incident windows.
- Author: implemented rate-limits on replay_schedule (global cap + per-repo small window) and added tests.
- Diego: flagged telemetry naming conventions; requested that soft_fail_count be an explicit metric with tags for prompt_set_id and cohort.
- Author: updated instrumentation and added tracing hooks; ran end-to-end and included telemetry example in docs.
- CI: early runs showed an intermittent integration-test timeout on Windows runner; root cause was nondeterministic sleep in integration harness and a flake guard was added (deterministic clock). Subsequent runs passed.

CI summary:
- unit tests: pass
- lint: pass (black/flake8/ruff)
- integration: initially fail (timeout) -> fixed -> pass
- e2e matrix (nightly): pending at time of first review; later green after rerun

Deployment / rollout plan:
- Stage 1: merge in opt-in mode, enable smoothing for a small set of internal prompt-sets via feature flag. Monitor soft_fail metrics and backtest delta.
- Stage 2: enable deferred_fail_fast in non-blocking mode for all repo CI runs (collect telemetry only) for 2 weeks.
- Stage 3: escalate to blocking mode with conservative thresholds after observing stable telemetry (expected after ~3+ weeks).

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-2451: dashboard tile in Console for soft-fail timelines and replay coverage (tracked in linked_linear).
- A follow-up PR will add a UI toggle to enable smoothing per-prompt-set in the Console and export smoothing parameters in eval exports.

Notes for reviewers: this PR is intentionally scoped to algorithm and CI hook + tests; no UX changes are included. The defaults are conservative; ops can opt in more aggressive smoothing via eval.smoothing.smoothing_temperature and anchor_prior_decay flags.
